subject: 2024 Annual Surveillance Report Review
overview: The committee reviewed the 2024 Annual Surveillance Report regarding body-worn cameras and debated police protocols regarding federal immigration enforcement. Members discussed internal audit findings and approved a timeline for the council's consolidated reporting.

items.title: Presentation of 2024 Annual Surveillance Report
items.summary: Police Chief Buckley reported that officers recorded over 31,000 body-worn camera videos in 2024, noting that the program successfully met department objectives for documentation and evidence collection.

items.title: Internal Use and Access Audits
items.summary: Officers discussed audit findings revealing that while technical compliance is high, officers failed to advise civilians they were being recorded in approximately one-third of audited cases.

items.title: Inquiry into Federal Law Enforcement Operations
items.summary: Chief Buckley confirmed that federal agents used the police station parking lot for safety during an independent operation but declined council requests to establish a formal notification system for federal immigration activities due to safety and legal concerns.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents requested more detailed data on the race and ethnicity of individuals recorded and questioned the costs associated with redacting video footage for public records requests.

items.title: Motion for Council’s Annual Public Report
items.summary: The committee approved a motion for Councilor Collins to prepare the council's required annual public report for inclusion on the May 27 agenda to allow more time for constituent review.
